chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakil narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ishaq! Whoever performs one Tawaf around this House, Allah writes for him a thousand good deeds, erases a thousand bad deeds, raises him a thousand degrees, plants for him a thousand trees in Paradise, and writes for him the reward of freeing a thousand souls. Until when he reaches the Multazam, Allah opens for him eight gates of Paradise, and it is said to him: Enter through whichever one you wish.'

He said: I said, 'May I be your ransom, is all of this for whoever performs Tawaf?' He said: 'Yes. Shall I not inform you of what is better than this?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Whoever fulfills the need of his believing brother, Allah writes for him Tawaf until it reaches ten.'

key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَمِ: The Multazam (the spot between the Kaaba door and the foundation stone)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fulfilling the needs of a believer compared to performing Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) quantifies the spiritual merit of a single circumambulation (Tawaf) as equivalent to a thousand good deeds, while emphasizing that fulfilling a believer's need yields the reward of ten Tawafs. This comparison underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on social solidarity and practical service (khidmah) as superior to ritual acts alone, reflecting the principle that the rights of people (huquq al-nas) are often more weighty than the rights of God (huquq Allah).

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 13. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ja’far who said it was narrated to me by Sahl b. Ziyad from Muhammad b. Ismail from Sa’dan b. Muslim from Ishaq b. Ammar who said:
“To one who fulfils a wish of a believer, Allah gives reward of Tawaaf, Tawaaf, Tawaaf…(he repeated it ten times).”
